title: Zscaler Posture Control (ZPC) and Cloud Protection: what ZPC covered, and its end of life

prose.label: End of life.
prose.text: {{zpc-eos-eol}} {{zcspm-eos-eol}} The DSPM offering it points to is in [[dspm.overview]]. Whether the product messaging narrowed with it is open {{gap:cnapp-redirect}}.

prose.label: How it works.
prose.text: {{zpc-access-and-scanning}} Whether it covers clouds beyond those named is open {{gap:cnapp-agentless}}. {{zpc-integrations}} How each integration works is open {{gap:cnapp-integration}}. {{zpc-threat-intel}} Whether it correlates misconfigurations into attack paths is open {{gap:cnapp-attack-paths}}.

prose.label: Cloud Protection.
prose.text: Whether Cloud Protection is a pillar that combines CSPM, microsegmentation and workload traffic security is open {{gap:cp-pillar}}. Whether it differs from Cloud Connector by scanning configuration rather than forwarding traffic is open {{gap:cp-vs-connector}}. The Cloud & Branch Connector product is in [[cloud-connector.overview]]. Where these captures came from is recorded in {{gap:cp-capture}}.

checks.do: Do not attribute CNAPP or posture-control behavior to DSPM or Cloud Connector; answer that the behavior is open and name the gap.

zpc-what.statement: Zscaler Posture Control (ZPC) is a multi-tenant software-as-a-service (SaaS) platform that detects and responds to cloud security risks, and is part of Zscaler Cloud Protection, which the page describes as a multi-cloud security platform covering misconfigurations, entitlements, exposed attack surfaces, lateral threat movement and data loss.

quotes: Zscaler Posture Control (ZPC) is a multi-tenant software-as-a-service (SaaS) platform that detects and responds to cloud security risks
ZPC is part of Zscaler Cloud Protection, a comprehensive multi-cloud security platform covering misconfigurations, entitlements, exposed attack surfaces, lateral threat movement, and data loss.

zpc-point-products.statement: ZPC comprises functionality previously covered by several point products, including Cloud Security Posture Management (CSPM), Cloud Infrastructure Entitlement Management (CIEM), Security and Compliance, Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) Security and Vulnerability Management.

quotes: ZPC comprises functionality previously covered by several point products, including:
Cloud Security Posture Management (CSPM): Ensure cloud resources have proper configurations
Cloud Infrastructure Entitlement Management (CIEM): Identify and remediate excessive permissions
Security and Compliance: Benchmark and validate public cloud configurations
Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) Security: Monitor your IaC infrastructure
Vulnerability Management: Monitor and detect any known vulnerabilities

zpc-access-and-scanning.statement: ZPC works with read-only access to AWS, Azure and Google Cloud environments, with read-write permission needed for vulnerability scanning, and scans container images in registries and VMs in production with an API-based, agentless approach. The page's introduction says ZPC continuously monitors cloud resources and detects vulnerabilities, DevOps misconfigurations and threats once business applications are deployed in the cloud infrastructure across AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud Platform and Kubernetes.

quotes: Works with read-only access to cloud environments (AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud).
However, you need read-write permission for vulnerability scanning.
Avoids developer friction and blind spots with an API-based, agentless approach. ZPC scans container images in registries and VMs in production environments to identify and prioritize risk.
once the business applications are deployed in the cloud infrastructure across Amazon Web Services (AWS), Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud Platform (GCP), and Kubernetes.
ZPC continuously monitors your cloud resources and detects vulnerabilities in your cloud resources, misconfigurations in DevOps workflow
as well as threats like ransomware attacks, account takeover, privilege escalation, etc.

zpc-integrations.statement: The page says ZPC integrates with the existing security operations (SecOps) ecosystem and IT service management (ITSM), and monitors automated deployment processes, alerting on critical security issues in CI/CD tools such as Jenkins and GitHub Actions and code repositories such as GitLab and GitHub.

quotes: Easily integrate with the existing security operations (SecOps) ecosystem and information technology service management (ITSM), and enable immediate and effective incident management.
ZPC monitors automated deployment processes and sends alerts when it identifies critical security issues in CI/CD tools like Jenkins, GitHub actions, and code repositories like GitLab and GitHub.

zpc-threat-intel.statement: ZPC uses threat intelligence from the Zscaler ThreatLabz research team to block malicious activity and future attack paths.

quotes: Leverages threat intelligence from the Zscaler ThreatLabz research team to gain a holistic view of the threat landscape and block malicious activity and future attack paths.

zpc-eos-eol.statement: Zscaler announced on December 17, 2024 the End-of-Sale of ZPC on March 15, 2025 and its End-of-Life planned for March 15, 2026, with existing tenants supported until the EOL, and recommends that ZPC users consider a migration plan to Zscaler Data Security Posture Management (DSPM).

quotes: | EOS Date | EOL Date |
The ZPC service and all existing tenants will be supported until the EOL of ZPC planned for March 15, 2026.
If you are using ZPC, you should consider a migration plan to Zscaler Data Security Posture Management (DSPM)
Announcement date: December 17, 2024

zcspm-eos-eol.statement: Zscaler Cloud Security Posture Management (ZCSPM) reached End-of-Sale on October 18, 2022 and End-of-Life on March 31, 2024; its notice pointed ZCSPM users to ZPC as the new generation platform covering ZCSPM functionality.

quotes: | EOS Date | EOL Date |
| October 18, 2022 | March 31, 2024 |
If you are using ZCSPM, you should consider a migration plan to Zscaler Posture Control (ZPC)—the new generation platform, covering ZCSPM functionality

cp-capture.title: Whether any captured page describes Cloud Protection, Posture Control or CNAPP
cp-capture.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Cloud Protection / Zero Trust Cloud ... Awareness only — no dedicated capture beyond the marketing-page references.' Searches of vendor/zscaler-help and vendor/zscaler-api-specs for CNAPP, CSPM, CIEM, Posture Control and Cloud Protection find no product page. The CSPM matches are admin role names in the ZIA and Cloud & Branch Connector API specs, not this offering.
cp-capture.resolution: The help site's Posture Control section is captured (the zpc-* pages, a lower tier) with the ZPC and ZCSPM End-of-Sale and End-of-Life notices; the overview and notices are cited by zpc-what, zpc-point-products, zpc-access-and-scanning, zpc-integrations, zpc-threat-intel, zpc-eos-eol and zcspm-eos-eol.

cp-pillar.title: Whether Cloud Protection is a platform pillar combining CSPM, microsegmentation and workload traffic
cp-pillar.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Pillar offering combining CSPM, microsegmentation, and secure east-west / ingress-egress traffic for workloads in AWS / Azure / on-prem. Marketed as a platform pillar rather than a discrete product.' No captured page describes this pillar.

cp-vs-connector.title: How Cloud Protection differs from Cloud Connector
cp-vs-connector.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Cloud Connector forwards workload traffic; Cloud Protection scans cloud configuration.' No captured page makes this distinction.

cnapp-convergence.title: What the Posture Control CNAPP converges
cnapp-convergence.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'The standalone Cloud Native Application Protection Platform (CNAPP) converges CSPM + CIEM + CWPP + DLP + IaC security + vulnerability management + compliance into one unified platform.' No captured page lists these components.
cnapp-convergence.resolution: ZPC names CSPM, CIEM, Security and Compliance, IaC Security and Vulnerability Management (zpc-point-products). CWPP and DLP are not named as products it comprises.

cnapp-agentless.title: Whether Posture Control scans agentlessly across four clouds
cnapp-agentless.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Agentless: API-based scan of container images in registries and VMs in production. Multi-cloud (AWS, Azure, GCP, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure).' No captured page says this.
cnapp-agentless.resolution: ZPC scans container images and VMs agentlessly with read-only access to AWS, Azure and Google Cloud, and names Kubernetes (zpc-access-and-scanning). Oracle Cloud Infrastructure is not named.

cnapp-attack-paths.title: Whether Posture Control correlates misconfigurations into attack paths
cnapp-attack-paths.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Distinguishing capability: correlates seemingly-low-risk individual misconfigurations into composite high-risk attack paths.' The captured DSPM marketing page makes an attack-path correlation claim for DSPM, not for a CNAPP product, so the legacy statement is not supported for Posture Control.

cnapp-redirect.title: Whether Posture Control's identity has narrowed into DSPM and CNAPP messaging
cnapp-redirect.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Marketing page redirects to the broader DSPM / CNAPP messaging; Posture Control's standalone identity has narrowed.' No captured page records a redirect or a change of identity.
cnapp-redirect.resolution: ZPC reached End-of-Sale on March 15, 2025 with End-of-Life planned for March 15, 2026, and its notice points users to DSPM (zpc-eos-eol). Whether the marketing identity narrowed is not stated.

cnapp-integration.title: How Posture Control integrates with customer environments
cnapp-integration.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'No SDK surfaced; agentless API scanning is the integration model.' No captured page describes an integration model for Posture Control.
cnapp-integration.resolution: ZPC integrates with SecOps and ITSM and monitors CI/CD tools and code repositories (zpc-integrations); how each integration works is not stated.
